---
title: "P3 exercise — Interpret a carbon budget"
---

Use the [tutorial](index.qmd). Allow 50–60 minutes. The numbers below are
invented for classroom analysis; they are not predictions for any species.
Leave with a hand-drawn response plot and a whole-plant explanation.

## 1. Trace atoms, energy and compartments

Draw a chloroplast with thylakoids and stroma. Label where water supplies
electrons, oxygen is released, ATP/NADPH are generated and CO2 is fixed. Add a
mitochondrion and explain why it remains relevant in an illuminated leaf.
Correct the statement: “The leaf splits CO2 to release oxygen and stores
light directly as ATP for transport to roots.”

## 2. Plot the measured response

The same leaf is measured at each light level after an equilibration period.
Other chamber settings are held constant. Positive values indicate net uptake.

| Light (µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹) | Net CO2 exchange (µmol CO2 m⁻² s⁻¹) |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0 | −2 |
| 50 | 0 |
| 200 | 6 |
| 800 | 9 |

Plot points, label axes/units, identify the observed compensation condition
and describe the change in response per added light. What additional evidence
would you need to identify the high-light limitation? Do not fit a straight
line across the whole range or treat the four readings as four plants.

## 3. Keep units through the calculation

A leaf maintains net uptake of 6 µmol CO2 m⁻² s⁻¹ over 0.02 m² for 600 s.
Calculate total net uptake in µmol CO2, assuming the rate remains constant.
Explain why this does not by itself give whole-plant dry-mass gain.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Worked units

6 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × 0.02 m² × 600 s = 72 µmol CO2. Leaf area and time cancel.
Other organs respire; carbon may be exported or stored; biomass composition
and longer-term variation have not been measured.
:::

## 4. Compare strategies under specified conditions

Explain the advantage and cost of CO2 concentration in a C4 leaf under warm,
bright conditions. Compare spatial concentration with a CAM plant's typical
night/day separation. Propose one observation supporting CAM, and one reason
that an overnight gas-exchange trace alone may need further verification.

## 5. Sources, sinks and nitrogen

During seed filling, a mature leaf exports carbon to developing seeds. Later,
a stored underground organ supports regrowth. Draw each source–sink relation.
Explain why “phloem carries sugar downwards” fails in at least one case.
Predict why severely oxygen-limited roots may have poor nutrient uptake even
when shoot photosynthesis continues. Connect carbon skeletons and energy to
nitrogen assimilation rather than treating nutrient supply as independent.

## Completion check

Distinguish gross component processes from net exchange; amount from rate;
photorespiration from mitochondrial respiration; source role from organ name.
Continue with the [self-check](quiz.qmd).
